findings: Shared BaseGun use-tick method calls virtual fireGun and only enters success handling when it returns true
Successful server-player path invokes doRecoil after damage/stat/cooldown handling
GunRecoilPacket serializes only recoilAmount float and firingTime int
Packet has no weapon-instance ID, hand, configuration revision or shot ordinal
The inspected doRecoil path sends to the firing player, not an identified observer/tracking broadcast
The client packet handler calls ClientOperations.addRecoil; treating this as a complete animation identity event is unsafe after swaps/offhand changes
Soul Storm belongs to BaseBlaster path, not BaseGun recoil path
BaseBlaster.tryFireBlaster can return true when fireBlaster returns null ShotInfo; doFiringEffects is therefore not a universal success signal
LightSpark and SoulSpark override use-tick but still call the inherited common tryFireBlaster gate
proposal: Two distinct source-audited adapter candidates: successful virtual fireGun branch inside the shared BaseGun use-tick path, and successful return from BaseBlaster.tryFireBlaster. Preserve original logic and validate actual runtime mixins/prediction/identity/observer routing before acceptance.
